newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta believes PCBs released in plant blast.
newsitem.headline: Alberta believes PCBs released in plant blast.

text.p: The Alberta government said late Wedensday it believed a stew of toxic chemicals was released into the atmosphere when an incinerator at the Swan Hills waste treatment plant exploded this week.
The blast at the northern Alberta plant, operated by Bovar Inc, occurred on Monday when vapors from a load of oilfield waste ignited.
Alberta's Environmental Protection ministry said it believed chemicals released included polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), dioxins and furans.

The explosion was the second incident in less than a year at the facility. Last December, Alberta laid charges against Bovar and ordered the company to step up the monitoring of emissions at the plant after a release of emissions resulted in toxins being found in animals in the region.
The government said late Wednesday that preliminary analysis of air quality samples around the plant were expected by the end of this week. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
